_: Declared quality gates for this project — the thresholds every actor (any agent, any tier, any human) must clear, held by quality_ratchet.py. STARTS EMPTY ON PURPOSE: a ratchet begins where the project IS, not where an article says it should be. Measure first, then declare each gate at its current value; `python3 quality_ratchet.py --run` reports every gate, and `install-hook` makes the pre-commit ratchet refuse any later commit that loosens one. Thresholds only tighten. Loosening one is a plan-mode decision made in its own commit with the reason in the ledger, committed with --no-verify — a recorded bypass, not an exemption (SAFEGUARDS.md Blast Radius Limits; SESSION_RUNNER.md failure mode #17; ITERATIVE_METHODOLOGY.md §Mechanical Gates Bind Every Actor).
_results_file: Where --run writes its results (gitignored by default — add it to .gitignore; the receipt cites the summary line, and the dashboard reads the file where it exists). Commit it instead if you want every clone to score the last run.
_gate_schema: Each gate: `name` (unique; the ratchet keys on it), `direction` (`min`: measured >= threshold, or `max`: measured <= threshold), `threshold` (a number), and optionally `command` (run via the shell from the project root) plus `extract` (a regex whose FIRST capture group is the measured number; without `extract` the command's exit code is the measurement, so `max 0` means `must exit 0`). A gate with no command is declared, not measured: --run reports it UNMEASURED and exits 1 — never pass. `why` and `unit` are free text for the reader.
